tools.name: get_spot_rate
tools.description: Get an indicative spot FX rate for a currency pair. Returns rounded bid, ask, and mid rates for illustration purposes only — not for execution. Example: base=GBP, quote=USD returns the GBPUSD rate.

tools.name: list_supported_currencies
tools.description: List the currency pairs currently available for Guard pricing. Always call this rather than assuming which pairs are supported — the list is configuration-driven and changes.

tools.name: get_forward_rate
tools.description: Use when you need a forward FX rate. tenor accepts either a period such as 1W, 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, or an exact date in ISO form YYYY-MM-DD. Use an exact date whenever you need the forward for the same day a Guard settles: a period resolves to the forward curve's own date, which can be several days away,

tools.name: price_guard
tools.description: Price a Guard — CurrencyGuard's FX protection product for real future payments or receipts. If a tenor like '3 months' is given, call resolve_settlement_date first to get the exact date, then call this tool. Returns: guardType (Guard-Pay or Guard-Receive), guardRate, guardFee (in the home currency),

tools.name: compare_guard_with_forward
tools.description: Use when a user asks whether a Guard is worth it, how it compares with a forward contract from their bank or provider, or what happens if they do nothing. ASK BEFORE YOU CALL. tools.name: resolve_settlement_date
tools.description: Resolve a relative time period (tenor) to a valid business settlement date for a currency pair. Use this when a user says '3 months', '6 months', '1 year', etc. instead of an exact date. The tenor format is: 1D (days), 1W (weeks), 1M (months), 1Y (years). Examples: '3M' = 3 months, '6M' = 6 months,

tools.description: Explain the Guard product using CurrencyGuard's approved product and FAQ content. Covers: what the Guard is, how it works, who it is for, how it compares to forwards or options, and legal, regulatory, accounting, or eligibility questions.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "net_exposure" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_forward_rate" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Get an indicative forward FX rate for a currency pair at a specific tenor. Rates are derived from interest rate differentials, rounded, and for illustration purposes only — not for execution. Returns: forwardRate (indicative mid outright = spot + forward points), forwardPoints (in pips, e.g. -3.1 me" → after: "Use when you need a forward FX rate. tenor accepts either a period such as 1W, 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, or an exact date in ISO form YYYY-MM-DD. Use an exact date whenever you need the forward for the same day a Guard settles: a period resolves to the forward curve's own date, which can be several days away,"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
